issues.text: Too absolute for this code. Private setters stop C# code from assigning Quantity, but stage-3 DonHangDbContext.cs:12 exposes `public DbSet<OrderItem> OrderItems`, and EF Core's change tracker (or ExecuteUpdate on that set) can still change a quantity without Order. Same wording in summary 3 ('a checked quantity cannot drop to 0 later') and quiz q4 explanation ('no code outside `OrderItem` can lower the quantity').
issues.quote: Once `Order` has checked an item, no code outside `OrderItem` can change its quantity.
issues.fix: s4: "Once `Order` has checked an item, no code outside `OrderItem` can assign its quantity." Summary 3: "...has no public setters, so no other class can assign a checked quantity again." Quiz q4 explanation (en+vi): "no code outside `OrderItem` can assign a new quantity to an item `Order` has already checked."

issues.text: Implies Order offers a way to change an item. At stage-3 no Order member changes an item after the constructor (claim 3; s4 itself says 'none of them adds or removes an item'), so 'ask the order' has nothing to call.
issues.quote: To change anything about an item through `IOrderRepository`, code has to load its order and ask the order.
issues.fix: Replace with "Through `IOrderRepository`, code reaches an item only by loading its order, and at stage-3 the order offers no method that changes an item."
